Estimate a reduced-form VAR by least squares

Source: R/varm.R
varm.Rd

Equation-by-equation OLS (identical to Gaussian ML for the coefficients) of $$y_t = c + \sum_{l=1}^p A_l y_{t-l} + \Gamma w_t + u_t,\quad u_t \sim (0,\Sigma).$$ The estimation loop is compiled (RcppArmadillo).

varm(Y, p = 1L, const = TRUE, trend = FALSE, exog = NULL)

Arguments

Y

numeric matrix, data frame or ts (T x K) of endogenous variables.

p

lag order.

const

include a constant.

trend

include a linear trend.

exog

optional T x q matrix of exogenous regressors (contemporaneous, treated like deterministic terms; future values are then required for forecasting).

Value

an object of class varm with elements B (m x K coefficient matrix, lags first then deterministics), Sigma (degrees-of-freedom corrected), U residuals, XtXinv, logLik and metadata.

Details

See vignette("var-theory") for definitions and the economic reading of the estimates.

Examples

fit <- varm(yraw, p = 2)
fit
#> <varm> VAR(2) with 3 variables, 213 effective observations
#> logLik = -338.416; max |eigenvalue| = 0.946
#> 
#>            X1      X2      X3
#> X1.l1  1.5378 -0.0095  0.5457
#> X2.l1 -0.2809  1.3297 -0.6475

#> X3.l2  0.0580  0.0457  0.1232
#> const  0.2872  0.3654  0.0052
summary(fit)
